sentences.text: Mr. Deshmukh, learned counsel for the appellant submits that it is not in dispute that the deceased was traveling in a truck, which is a goods vehicle and that he was a gratuitous passenger.
sentences._hearing_file: New India Assurance Co. Ltd, Mumbai vs Namdeo Tukaram Kale And Others on 7 October, 2025.json

sentences.text: He further submits that the said truck turned turtle resulting in the death of Balu Kale due to injuries sustained in the accident.
sentences._hearing_file: New India Assurance Co. Ltd, Mumbai vs Namdeo Tukaram Kale And Others on 7 October, 2025.json

sentences.text: The legal representatives of the deceased filed the claim petition.
sentences._hearing_file: New India Assurance Co. Ltd, Mumbai vs Namdeo Tukaram Kale And Others on 7 October, 2025.json

sentences.text: Mr. Deshmukh submits that the Insurance Company in its written statement specifically raised the objection that the risk of a gratuitous passenger traveling in a goods vehicle is not covered under the policy of insurance.
sentences._hearing_file: New India Assurance Co. Ltd, Mumbai vs Namdeo Tukaram Kale And Others on 7 October, 2025.json

sentences.text: Despite accepting this defense, the learned Tribunal while dismissing the claim against the appellant-Insurance Company, nevertheless directed the Insurance Company to first pay the compensation amount to the claimants and thereafter recover the same from the insured owner of the vehicle.
sentences._hearing_file: New India Assurance Co. Ltd, Mumbai vs Namdeo Tukaram Kale And Others on 7 October, 2025.json

sentences.text: Mr. Deshmukh contends that such a direction was without jurisdiction.
sentences._hearing_file: New India Assurance Co. Ltd, Mumbai vs Namdeo Tukaram Kale And Others on 7 October, 2025.json

sentences.text: He submits that this is not a case involving breach of the terms or conditions of the policy, but rather a case where the risk itself is not covered (3) 915 FA1361 OF 2014 under the policy.
sentences._hearing_file: New India Assurance Co. Ltd, Mumbai vs Namdeo Tukaram Kale And Others on 7 October, 2025.json

sentences.text:
He opposes the impugned direction on two grounds:
(i) When the risk is not covered at all, and it is not a case of breach of policy, the direction to "pay and recover" cannot be issued and (ii) Such directions are beyond the jurisdiction of the Tribunal, as the power to issue "pay and recover" directions in such cases lies exclusively with the Hon'ble Supreme Court under Article 142 of the Constitution of India.
sentences._hearing_file: New India Assurance Co. Ltd, Mumbai vs Namdeo Tukaram Kale And Others on 7 October, 2025.json

sentences.text: 4. Mr. Hange, learned counsel for the claimants, submits that the Tribunal has rightly issued the said directions keeping in view the object and spirit of this social welfare legislation.
sentences._hearing_file: New India Assurance Co. Ltd, Mumbai vs Namdeo Tukaram Kale And Others on 7 October, 2025.json

sentences.text: He further submits that in several similar cases, both this Court and the Hon'ble Supreme Court have issued such directions even in cases where the deceased was a gratuitous occupant in a goods vehicle.
sentences._hearing_file: New India Assurance Co. Ltd, Mumbai vs Namdeo Tukaram Kale And Others on 7 October, 2025.json

sentences.text: He states that he shall be ready for final hearing of the appeal within two weeks.
sentences._hearing_file: New India Assurance Co. Ltd, Mumbai vs Namdeo Tukaram Kale And Others on 7 October, 2025.json

sentences.text:
5. In view of this and by consent of both the parties, list this matter on 10.11.2025.

sentences.text:
This appeal, at the instance of original respondent no.2 arises out of judgment and award dated 09.05.2014 passed by learned M.A.C.T. Beed, in M.A.C.P. No. 147 of 2005 awarding maintenance to the original claimants/respondent Nos.2 to 5 herein, on account of accidental death of Balu Namdeo Kale, who died in road traffic accident dated 03.01.2005.
2.
sentences._hearing_file: New India Assurance Co. Ltd, Mumbai vs Namdeo Tukaram Kale And Others on 22 December, 2025.json

sentences.text:
In nutshell, present respondent nos.1 to 5, who are original claimants, instituted above M.A.C.P.,
on the premise that, deceased Balu, who was a labourer engaged in sugarcane cutting, was traveling in a truck bearing No. MH-15-G-2827, which was meant for transporting sugarcane labourers on behalf of sugar factory.
sentences._hearing_file: New India Assurance Co. Ltd, Mumbai vs Namdeo Tukaram Kale And Others on 22 December, 2025.json

sentences.text: On the said day, driver of the vehicle i.e. respondent no.1 was driving the vehicle in rash and negligent manner, as a result of which, the vehicle turned turtle causing fatal injuries to the deceased, due to which, he died.
sentences._hearing_file: New India Assurance Co. Ltd, Mumbai vs Namdeo Tukaram Kale And Others on 22 December, 2025.json

sentences.text: Therefore, invoking section 163-A of the Motor FA-1361-2014 Vehicles Act, heirs of deceased Balu set up accident claim for compensation, which was contested by present appellant i.e. original respondent no.2.
sentences._hearing_file: New India Assurance Co. Ltd, Mumbai vs Namdeo Tukaram Kale And Others on 22 December, 2025.json

sentences.text: Ultimately, learned tribunal allowed the claim petition directing compensation to the tune of Rs.4,00,000/- to be paid by original respondent no.1 with interest.
sentences._hearing_file: New India Assurance Co. Ltd, Mumbai vs Namdeo Tukaram Kale And Others on 22 December, 2025.json

sentences.text: However, there were further directions by order dated 09.05.2014 that, present appellant (original respondent no.2 insurance company) to satisfy the award and then recover it from respondent no.1.
sentences._hearing_file: New India Assurance Co. Ltd, Mumbai vs Namdeo Tukaram Kale And Others on 22 December, 2025.json

sentences.text: Dissatisfied by the above order of 'pay and recover', insurance company has come up in appeal.
sentences._hearing_file: New India Assurance Co. Ltd, Mumbai vs Namdeo Tukaram Kale And Others on 22 December, 2025.json

sentences.text: 3. Heard.

sentences.text: Learned counsel for insurance company Shri Deshmukh would raise fundamental objection to the grant of compensation.
sentences._hearing_file: New India Assurance Co. Ltd, Mumbai vs Namdeo Tukaram Kale And Others on 22 December, 2025.json

sentences.text:
According to him, the vehicle being goods vehicle, deceased being gratuitous passenger, he was not entitled to travel therein and no extra premium being paid,
the insurance company was not liable.
sentences._hearing_file: New India Assurance Co. Ltd, Mumbai vs Namdeo Tukaram Kale And Others on 22 December, 2025.json

sentences.text: It is his submission that, when learned tribunal had clearly recorded a finding that insurance company succeeded in proving that there was breach of policy and not liable to pay, learned tribunal ought not to have even directed insurance company to first pay and then recover later.
sentences._hearing_file: New India Assurance Co. Ltd, Mumbai vs Namdeo Tukaram Kale And Others on 22 December, 2025.json

sentences.text: It is also his submission that, though precedents laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court are regarding pay and recover, it is his specific submission that, this has been done FA-1361-2014 by the Hon'ble Apex court in exercise of Article 142 of the Constitution of India, and therefore, it is not open for this court to direct pay and recover.

sentences.text: The purpose of an insurance policy in the present context is to shield the owner/operator from direct liability when such an unforeseen/unfortunate incident takes place.

sentences.text:
To deny the victim/dependents of the victim compensation simply because the accident took place outside the bounds of the permit and,
therefore, is outside the purview of the insurance policy, would be offensive to the sense of justice, for the accident itself is for no fault of his.

sentences.text: Then, the Insurance Company most certainly ought to pay.

sentences.text: The contract lays down the four corners within which such an insurance policy would operate.

opennyai_summary.7_October_2025__facts:
Feeling aggrieved by the judgment and decree dated 09.05.2014 passed by the learned Member,
Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Beed in Motor Accident Claim Petition No.147 of 2005, the appellant/Insurance Company has raised this appeal under Section 173 of the Motor Vehicles Act,
New India Assurance Co. Ltd, Mumbai vs Namdeo Tukaram Kale And Others on 7 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/13101188/
1 1988.
3.
opennyai_summary.7_October_2025__arguments:
Mr. Deshmukh, learned counsel for the appellant submits that it is not in dispute that the deceased was traveling in a truck, which is a goods vehicle and that he was a gratuitous passenger.
The legal representatives of the deceased filed the claim petition.
Mr. Deshmukh submits that the Insurance Company in its written statement specifically raised the objection that the risk of a gratuitous passenger traveling in a goods vehicle is not covered under the policy of insurance.
Despite accepting this defense, the learned Tribunal while dismissing the claim against the appellant-Insurance Company, nevertheless directed the Insurance Company to first pay the compensation amount to the claimants and thereafter recover the same from the insured owner of the vehicle.
He opposes the impugned direction on two grounds:
(i) When the risk is not covered at all, and it is not a case of breach of policy, the direction to "pay and recover" cannot be issued and (ii) Such directions are beyond the jurisdiction of the Tribunal, as the power to issue "pay and recover" directions in such cases lies exclusively with the Hon'ble Supreme Court under Article 142 of the Constitution of India.
opennyai_summary.7_October_2025__decision: He states that he shall be ready for final hearing of the appeal within two weeks.

opennyai_summary.final__facts:
In nutshell, present respondent nos.1 to 5, who are original claimants, instituted above M.A.C.P.,
on the premise that, deceased Balu, who was a labourer engaged in sugarcane cutting, was traveling in a truck bearing No. MH-15-G-2827, which was meant for transporting sugarcane labourers on behalf of sugar factory.
On the said day, driver of the vehicle i.e. respondent no.1 was driving the vehicle in rash and negligent manner, as a result of which, the vehicle turned turtle causing fatal injuries to the deceased, due to which, he died.
Therefore, invoking section 163-A of the Motor FA-1361-2014 Vehicles Act, heirs of deceased Balu set up accident claim for compensation, which was contested by present appellant i.e. original respondent no.2.
Ultimately, learned tribunal allowed the claim petition directing compensation to the tune of Rs.4,00,000/- to be paid by original respondent no.1 with interest.
However, there were further directions by order dated 09.05.2014 that, present appellant (original respondent no.2 insurance company) to satisfy the award and then recover it from respondent no.1.
opennyai_summary.final__arguments:
According to him, the vehicle being goods vehicle, deceased being gratuitous passenger, he was not entitled to travel therein and no extra premium being paid,
the insurance company was not liable.
It is his submission that, when learned tribunal had clearly recorded a finding that insurance company succeeded in proving that there was breach of policy and not liable to pay, learned tribunal ought not to have even directed insurance company to first pay and then recover later.
In support of above contentions, learned counsel seeks reliance on the judgments of this court in First Appeal No.1502 of 2018, decided on 07.02.2024 in the case of New India Assurance Company Ltd. v. Manoj Gangaram Narwade and Ors. ; in First Appeal No. 1401 of 2004 with connected First New India Assurance Co. Ltd, Mumbai vs Namdeo Tukaram Kale And Others on 22 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/193748970/
2 Appeal Nos. 1403 of 2004 and 1406 of 2004, decided on 21.02.2024 in the case of The New India Assurance Company Ltd. v. Nagesh s/o. Niloba Deshmukh as well as in First Appeal No. 1804 of 2018 decided on 22.10.2019 in the case of Shriram General Insurance Company Ltd. v. Laxman Manik Jadhav and Ors. and New India Assurance Co. Ltd. v. Asha Rani and Ors., (2001) 6 SCC 724.
4.
In answer to above submission, learned counsel Shri Hange for respondents/Orig. claimants would point out that, in this case, though deceased was declared to be a gratuitous passenger, he justifies order of grant of pay and recover and in support of such contention, he seeks reliance on the judgments of this court in the case of Shivaraj v. Rajendra and Anr., (2019) 4 Mh.L.J. 16.; Manuara Khatun and Ors. v. Rajesh Kumar Singh and Ors. (2017) 4 SCC 796; New India Assurance Co. Ltd. v.
Bhagubai w/o. Tukaram FA-1361-2014 Margal and Ors. in First Appeal No. 479 of 2015; Brij Bihari Gupta v. Manmet & Ors., in Civil Appeal Nos.6338-6339 of 2024 (Supreme Court); Sunita and Ors.
v. United Insurance Company Ltd. and ors .; AIR Online 2025 SC 601; and lastly Kurvan Ansari alias Kurvan Ali and Anr. v. Shyam Kishore Murmu & Anr. in Civil Appeal No.6902 of 2024 (Supreme Court).
5.
The primary objection raised was that, the vehicle was driven in breach of the terms and conditions of policy as it was a goods vehicle, in which the travel or journey by persons was not permitted and hence, case was set up that liability cannot be fastened.
opennyai_summary.issue:
The only question which this court is called upon to address is whether, when the insurance company is not liable to indemnify the claim of a gratuitous passenger for traveling in a goods vehicle, an order of "Pay and Recover" can at all be passed.
6. Heard.

passed by learned tribunal, is justified and is consequently required FA-1361-2014 to be upheld.
